## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṅgahavāra* ("Comprehensive Section") constitutes the opening portion of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Netti) [Hinüber 1996]. It is an extremely brief text consisting of only five verses that mention the name of Mahākaccāna, who is traditionally regarded in the Theravāda tradition as the author of the Netti [Hinüber 1996]. The subsequent *Uddesavāra* ("specification section"), which begins the *vibhāga* and enumerates the sixteen *hāras*, five *nayas*, and eighteen *mūlapadas*, functions in part as a concise commentary upon this *Saṅgahavāra* [Hinüber 1996].

 Machine text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus records six internal Pali textual matches with the subcommentarial *Nettivibhāvinī* (Tika S0501t), predominantly covering segments §1.1–1.4, while yielding no cross-language matches above threshold [DharmaNexus].
